name: Holiness roots
description: The nineteenth-century Holiness environment helped shape emerging Pentecostal revivals. The year 1900 is an approximate turn-of-century influence marker, not a legal founding event; Topeka followed in 1901 and Azusa in 1906.
narrative: The nineteenth-century Holiness environment helped shape emerging Pentecostal revivals. The year 1900 is an approximate turn-of-century influence marker, not a legal founding event; Topeka followed in 1901 and Azusa in 1906. Pentecostal revival grew from several evangelical and Holiness environments. Charles Parham’s Topeka circle in 1901 and William Seymour’s Azusa Street revival from 1906 became influential American centers, but no single institution founded every global Pentecostal stream. Some older Holiness churches later adopted Pentecostal teaching. Trinitarian and Oneness traditions, and Wesleyan and Finished Work accounts of sanctification, demonstrate the movement’s internal diversity.

key_figures.summary: A revival teacher associated with the Topeka Bible school and an influential formulation of tongues as evidence of Spirit baptism; he did not found every Pentecostal stream.

name: Pentecostal denomination formed
description: Assemblies of God organized in 1914 as a Pentecostal denomination.
narrative: Assemblies of God organized in 1914 as a Pentecostal denomination. Ministers gathered at Hot Springs, Arkansas, to coordinate a rapidly expanding Pentecostal network. E. N. Bell and J. Roswell Flower were elected early officers. The adoption of the Statement of Fundamental Truths in 1916 clarified a Trinitarian doctrinal basis. The United States body is part of a wider world fellowship of national organizations; global membership should not be mistaken for membership of the American General Council.

name: Later Pentecostal identity of an older church
description: The church traces its institutional foundation to an 1886 Christian Union, before the Pentecostal movement marker used here. It later developed Holiness-Pentecostal teaching. This undated influence edge records religious development rather than formation by a future parent.
narrative: The church traces its institutional foundation to an 1886 Christian Union, before the Pentecostal movement marker used here. It later developed Holiness-Pentecostal teaching. This undated influence edge records religious development rather than formation by a future parent. Richard Green Spurling and a small community organized a Christian Union in 1886 seeking New Testament fellowship. Later Holiness revival and Pentecostal experience changed its religious life; the name Church of God was adopted in 1907. Under A. J. Tomlinson the movement expanded organization and mission. Its 1886 foundation therefore precedes the 1906 Azusa marker used for the Pentecostal movement node.

name: Mason adopts Pentecostal teaching
description: COGIC’s name dates to 1897; Mason’s 1907 Azusa experience and subsequent division with Jones mark its Pentecostal development. The edge records adoption and influence, not founding of the earlier Holiness body.
narrative: COGIC’s name dates to 1897; Mason’s 1907 Azusa experience and subsequent division with Jones mark its Pentecostal development. The edge records adoption and influence, not founding of the earlier Holiness body. Charles Harrison Mason and Charles Price Jones worked in a Holiness revival setting after conflict with Baptist churches. The Church of God in Christ name dates to 1897. Mason’s 1907 visit to Azusa Street and his acceptance of Pentecostal teaching led to a division with Jones. Mason’s followers retained the COGIC name and built an episcopally organized church with national institutions in Memphis.

name: Reported AG separation: institutional relationship unresolved
description: Foursquare’s 1923 Angelus Temple beginning is documented, but the official history consulted does not establish a direct denomination-wide split from Assemblies of God. The inherited split assertion remains a low-confidence hypothesis pending direct evidence.
narrative: Foursquare’s 1923 Angelus Temple beginning is documented, but the official history consulted does not establish a direct denomination-wide split from Assemblies of God. The inherited split assertion remains a low-confidence hypothesis pending direct evidence. McPherson established Los Angeles as a base for evangelism, opened Angelus Temple in 1923, and developed training, church planting, radio, and overseas mission. Incorporation steps followed in 1927 after a wider network had formed. Its name expresses a fourfold presentation of Jesus. Personal connections with other Pentecostal ministries do not by themselves prove that the entire body was created by an institutional split from the Assemblies of God.
